# BugIt

> BugIt is a QA agent made by Taskivator. It runs inside the AI assistant you already use (GitHub Copilot Chat in VS Code, the Claude extension, or a terminal), turns a rough note into a complete bug report, and files it to your tracker, such as Jira, GitHub or Azure DevOps, only after you type FILE IT.

Your tickets, specs and settings go only to the tools you connect and the AI assistant you choose.

## Product

- [BugIt home](https://bugit.dev/): what BugIt does, how it works and pricing
- [Documentation](https://bugit.dev/docs/): install, activate, customize and use BugIt

## Articles

- [How to write a bug report](https://bugit.dev/articles/): the parts of a good report in the order you write them, with a deeper article for each step
- [A bug report template developers will actually read](https://bugit.dev/articles/bug-report-template-developers-read/): A copyable bug report template, what each part is for, and the habits that turn a vague complaint into a ticket a developer can fix.
- [Catch duplicate bugs before you file them](https://bugit.dev/articles/catch-duplicate-bugs-before-filing/): Why one bug turns into several tickets, how to search a tracker so you find the earlier one, and what to do when you do.
- [Reproduce a bug from a log file: a detective's guide](https://bugit.dev/articles/reproduce-a-bug-from-logs/): How to find the failing moment in a log, trim it to what matters, turn it into repeatable steps and share it safely.
- [How to report a bug that only happens sometimes](https://bugit.dev/articles/report-a-bug-that-only-happens-sometimes/): How to report an intermittent bug: count your runs, find what changes between them, and write the conditions down so a developer can chase it.
- [Screenshots and recordings that help fix the bug](https://bugit.dev/articles/screenshots-and-recordings-for-bug-reports/): What to capture in a bug report screenshot or recording, how to crop and annotate it, and how to keep personal data and secrets out of the picture.
- [A bug that used to work: how to report a regression](https://bugit.dev/articles/report-a-regression-bug/): How to report a regression: find the last version that worked, narrow the gap to the first one that failed, and give the developer a place to start.
- [Bug report templates for Jira, GitHub and Azure DevOps](https://bugit.dev/articles/bug-report-template-jira-github-azure-devops/): Free copy and paste bug report templates for Jira, GitHub Issues and Azure DevOps, including a GitHub issue form file you can add to a repository.
- [Find duplicate bugs: Jira, GitHub and Azure DevOps searches](https://bugit.dev/articles/search-for-duplicate-bugs-jira-github-azure-devops/): Copy and paste searches to find an existing bug before you file one: JQL for Jira, GitHub issue search qualifiers, and WIQL and search tips for Azure DevOps.
- [How to write reproduction steps: a checklist](https://bugit.dev/articles/how-to-write-reproduction-steps-checklist/): A short checklist for writing steps to reproduce a bug that a stranger can follow, with a before and after example and a template you can copy.
- [Severity vs priority: a bug triage matrix](https://bugit.dev/articles/severity-vs-priority-bug-triage-matrix/): What severity and priority mean in bug triage, how they differ, and a copyable matrix with examples to decide which bug gets fixed first.
- [Bug report examples: good and bad, side by side](https://bugit.dev/articles/bug-report-examples-good-and-bad/): Bug report examples, good and bad, side by side: four weak reports rewritten so a developer can act on them, with notes on what changed.
- [A bug triage checklist you can run in five minutes](https://bugit.dev/articles/bug-triage-checklist/): A bug triage checklist for a team: confirm the bug, check for duplicates, set severity and priority, assign an owner, and keep the meeting short.

## Free templates

- [Free bug report templates](https://bugit.dev/templates/): General bug report template, Jira bug report template, GitHub issue form, Azure DevOps bug template, Steps to reproduce checklist, Severity and priority guide, to copy or download. A template is the manual way: you fill in each box yourself. BugIt does the filling in for you, from a rough note.

## Free tools

- [Steps to reproduce checklist](https://taskivator.com/steps-to-reproduce-checklist/): A checklist and a live template you fill in and copy. It runs in your browser.
- [Bug severity helper](https://taskivator.com/bug-severity-helper/): Answer three questions and copy a suggested severity with its reason into your ticket.
- [Bug report template builder](https://taskivator.com/bug-report-template-builder/): Fill in the parts and copy a report laid out for Jira or Azure DevOps.
